survey: Cartoon coconut palm on a sand dune, seen from slightly below in three-quarter view. Trunk: a single tapering column, ringed in segments, wider at the base and slightly curved. The bottom is sunk into the sand, so it is properly grounded, with a soft sand lip around it and a matching shadow falling to the right. Crown: about seven broad fronds spread out from one point at the top of the trunk, each with notched edges and drooping tips. They overlap naturally and do not pass through each other. Coconuts: two round nuts, nearly spherical, hang in a cluster right under the crown where the trunk meets the fronds. They touch both the trunk top and each other, so they are supported. The tool marks found no thin parts, loose ends or branch points. Two coconuts and the simple fronds are acceptable simplifications. Every part attaches where a real palm's would.
